title: You are cosmic-ext-nightlight's Compliance check, for this one job: nobody else…
requests:
You are cosmic-ext-nightlight's Compliance check, for this one job: nobody else is working here now, so what you change can't collide with anyone. You work like an engineer, in your own worktree and branch; what you change is reviewed and merged like any other work. Check four things, fix what you can in your branch, and file an issue (create_issue) for each thing you can't fix in this one pass.

1. Code. Read the code changed since the last Compliance check (git log for the latest merge of a ferrivide/compliance- branch; the whole project if there's none) against the project's requirements (the ide tool's requirements action), the contract, and AGENTS.md's conventions: doc comments where they're asked for, no new clippy warnings (cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets, when it's a Rust project), the formatting the project uses. Check it reads well to a person: clear names, plain comments that say what and why, functions of a reasonable size. Rename, comment or split only where it clearly helps; don't rewrite working code to taste.
   Rust projects (a Cargo.toml) are also checked against the rust-development skill (RS1 to RS8, given to you in full): call the ide tool's rust_smells action with clippy: true, and with whole: true the first time (when no Compliance branch has merged) so the whole workspace is covered, every crate and app/ included. Later runs: your branch starts from the current tip, so the action's default scope (your change) is empty; find the last merged ferrivide/compliance- merge in git log, scan with whole: true, and keep only the findings in files changed since it (git diff --name-only <merge>..HEAD). Judge each finding against the standard it cites; a flag isn't always a fault. Fix the small, local ones in your branch (a clone that only ends a borrow, a needless allocation in a hot path, an `unsafe` without a SAFETY comment). For each cluster you can't fix in this one pass, file one issue (create_issue, with an area from the project's categories that fits the code concerned) saying which standard it breaks, how many findings there are, and their files and lines. Mark a structural one (a god struct, a monolith file or impl, a crate to split) "For the architect" in its title, as the architect picks those up. Before filing, read the open issues (list_issues) and file nothing for what one already covers. When the whole tree is scanned and a crate is very large (tens of thousands of lines, as Ferrivide's app/ is), measure the incremental check time (touch a file in it, then time cargo check -p <crate>, twice) and file an issue to split the crate only if those times support it, quoting them.
2. Scans. Call the ide tool's run_scanners action: Ferrivide runs its own RustSec scan and the vulnerability scanners that are installed (trivy, grype) on the project's checkout (what's merged, not your branch) and the toolchain, confined like your commands, and puts their findings in the CVE tab; you're sent their results when they're done (vulnerabilities shows them too). A fix on your branch shows as resolved only once it's merged and scanned again: say in your report which findings your branch fixes. Never install a scanner: if one is missing, say so in your report. While Ferrivide is offline, the scans use their cached databases: say how old each is.
3. CVEs. Every finding in vulnerabilities must be Fixed, or Not affected by a person's approval. For each still open, upgrade the dependency in your branch when that's a small, safe change; otherwise file an issue saying what's needed, or, when the project truly isn't affected, propose_not_affected with the reason (only the person can accept it).
4. Docs. Check that SECURITY.md, README.md, the release notes (RELEASES or CHANGELOG), PRIVACY.md, AGENTS.md and docs/ say what the code does now (network connections, what agents can reach, settings, commands), and that the requirements and features (requirements action) match what's built. Correct the docs in your branch; the requirements and features you only report, for the person who keeps them.

Leave alone what's another job: no new features, no speed work, no redesign. Run a command heavier than the default resource limits only after asking through C13.

Your closing report_status is published as your report, in the project's Reports tab (Compliance Check). Put in its summary a section for each: Code (what you checked and fixed; for Rust, the smell scan's counts by standard, the clippy flags, and each issue filed, with its id and whether it is for the architect), Scans (each scanner, its database date and how many findings, or that it's missing), CVEs (each open finding and what's done about it) and Docs (what didn't match and what you corrected); list your changes in its decisions and files. If nothing needs changing, commit nothing and say what you checked. Once your work is merged (or you finish with nothing to merge), you're discarded.

The user's direction for this start, as the project manager carries it (it comes first where it narrows the work):
Run the vulnerability scanners before the release (R34) and report findings.

Issues earmarked for the compliance (the project manager gave them to this position; no engineer takes them), each as it stands now:

[Issue FV-X6J1CF]
FV-X6J1CF: Run the vulnerability scanners before the release (R34): the CVE tab has never been scanned
Status: Backlog
Labels: Docs
Origin: made in Ferrivide by Engineer 1

Found by the release pass. The CVE tab (`vulnerabilities`) shows `scanned_at: null`, no RustSec cache date, no scanner results and `exploitation_status: unknown`. It also reports that OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, the Rust toolchain, build and release tools, and bundled assets have never been scanned. With no scan there is no evidence for R34 either way (no critical or actively exploited finding left unaddressed; R34 isn't among the recorded requirements yet).

Compliance: run `run_scanners` on the merged checkout (RustSec, plus trivy and grype if installed). Then fix any critical or actively exploited finding, or put it to the user as an exception. The release must wait for this.

Dependencies to keep in mind: git dependencies (libcosmic @8fa46cc, cosmic-panel @03c1358, window_clipboard tag sctk-0.20, dbus-settings-bindings, freedesktop-icons) aren't in the RustSec index by version, so a clean RustSec result doesn't cover them.

Findings that couldn't be resolved in that change (R24), each with why:

- [should_fix] docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md:21: The task asked to confirm Iced-Icons.ttf's origin and license upstream. The doc says this was not done (no network), so the row remains an open point and the package ships with an unverified font license. This must be closed before the release, not left to the reader.
  - Why it's left for later: it needs a decision from the user: Confirming Iced-Icons.ttf's upstream glyph license needs network access to iced-rs/iced and Fontello, which I don't have. Tracked as FV-MGVC59 and linked from docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md.
  - Suggested fix: Confirm with iced-rs/iced (the font's source and the glyph license, e.g. Fontello's MIT/OFL terms) and replace the 'Open point' text with the confirmed license and source. If it can't be confirmed before merge, record it as an open issue and link it from the doc.
  - Raised by Quick reviewer (Haiku 5.5) on Engineer 2's work on cosmic-ext-nightlight

Work on them along with the job above. For each one your work fixes, end the message of the commit that fixes it with a line "Fixes <its id>": its merge closes it. One you can't fix stays earmarked for this position's next start: say why in your closing report.

decisions.decision: Attributed Iced-Icons.ttf's glyphs to Font Awesome (OFL 1.1) by matching their outlines
decisions.why: The font's name table says only 'Fontello'. Glyph names were ambiguous between sets: down-dir and ok also exist in Entypo and Web Symbols. Advance widths and bounding boxes matched Font Awesome's src/svg files exactly, after the 850 ascent flip, and no other set's did.
alternatives: Leave the open point for the user (FV-MGVC59)
Assume from the glyph names alone

decisions.decision: Moved the Temperature and Applied branches of update into temperature_changed and reply_received
decisions.why: RS7 / clippy::too_many_lines (146 lines); the bodies are moved as they were, and tests and clippy pass.
alternatives: Leave it as a message dispatcher and file an issue

decisions.decision: Didn't change handle_request for the RS4 flag
decisions.why: GammaBackend::new runs only while there is no backend, once per connection, which isn't a hot path; the code already documents this.

decisions.decision: Closed FV-X6J1CF with this merge, and filed the coverage gaps as FV-YWGP02
decisions.why: The scan it asked for ran, with 0 findings. Installing trivy or grype is the user's decision, not something to hold the scan issue open for.

progress:
Compliance check (the first, so the whole tree): no open CVEs; trivy and grype aren't installed; Iced-Icons.ttf's licence traced to Font Awesome (OFL 1.1) and its notice now ships; `update` split for RS7. 46 tests pass.

**Code**: I checked the whole tree: `cargo fmt --check` passes and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` has no warnings. The smell scan with clippy found 2 findings. RS7: 1 (`update` in `src/main.rs:1002` was 146 lines); I fixed it by moving two of its branches into their own functions, with no change in behaviour. RS4: 1 (`src/main.rs:78`, `handle_request` called in the worker's loop) is a false positive: the backend is built only when there is no connection, and the code already says so. Nothing for RS1–RS3, RS5, RS6 or RS8. I filed no code issues and nothing for the architect. Requirements R1 and R2 hold: libcosmic applet, gamma set over Wayland with no external tools.

**Scans**: RustSec: 0 findings; its database was fetched online at 2026-11-14 05:57 UTC. trivy and grype are not installed, so they didn't run. Git dependencies (libcosmic, cosmic-panel, window_clipboard and others) aren't covered by RustSec, and OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, the toolchain and the release tools weren't scanned. Filed as FV-YWGP02 (Docs, a decision for the user: install trivy or grype).

**CVEs**: none open. R34 has nothing to fix, but only within the coverage above.

**Docs**: the README, CHANGELOG, docs/RELEASING.md and docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md match the code: the settings and their ranges, the 20-second check, the 60-minute ramp, zone.tab, and no network access. Corrected: BUNDLED-ASSETS.md's open point on Iced-Icons.ttf. Network was available, so I matched each glyph outline against Fontello's Font Awesome sources: six glyphs are Font Awesome (Dave Gandy, SIL OFL 1.1) and one is the iced logo (MIT). `data/licenses/OFL-FontAwesome.txt` is new and the .deb installs it (checked with `cargo deb` and `dpkg -c`). The CHANGELOG now lists the notices the package installs. There is no SECURITY.md, PRIVACY.md or AGENTS.md (reported, not created). For whoever keeps the requirements: issues cite R14, R33 and R34, but only R0–R2 are recorded, and the features miss Auto (sunrise/sunset) and the .deb/apt packaging.

Earmarked issues: FV-J3BMZE and FV-MGVC59 are fixed by this commit (the font licence). FV-X6J1CF is fixed (the scan ran), with the remaining gaps in FV-YWGP02.

reviews.summary: The change adds the Font Awesome OFL text and its packaging entry, corrects the Iced-Icons.ttf row in docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md, adds a CHANGELOG entry, and splits Nightlight::update's Temperature and Applied arms into temperature_changed and reply_received. I compared the two new functions line by line with the removed inline code: the logic is the same, and the std::mem::take of retune_pending is taken before check_auto runs and no call in between reads it. cargo test --locked passes (46 passed, 1 ignored), cargo fmt --check is clean, and clippy printed no warnings. The refactor adds no tests of its own, but the existing tests cover the paths it moved.
The refactor of `update` is behavior-preserving. The Font Awesome OFL file is installed in the .deb assets, and the docs and CHANGELOG match. Tests pass (46 passed, 1 ignored) and clippy is clean.

The change ships the Font Awesome OFL text as a 644 doc asset, updates BUNDLED-ASSETS.md and CHANGELOG, and moves two match arms of Nightlight::update into methods (temperature_changed, reply_received). The moved code is identical to the original. reply_received takes Result by reference, so nothing extra is cloned. The `mem::take` of `retune_pending` happens after the last call that could read it, so RS2 holds. It adds no I/O, input handling, unsafe code, dependencies or permission changes. 46 tests pass (1 ignored) and clippy reports no warnings.

learned: Packaging: Iced-Icons.ttf (compiled in by iced_graphics) holds six Font Awesome glyphs (SIL OFL 1.1, Dave Gandy, picked through Fontello) and the iced logo (MIT). Its OFL notice is data/licenses/OFL-FontAwesome.txt; re-check it if iced_graphics changes the font.
Packaging: cargo-deb 3.8.0 is installed here, so `cargo deb --locked` followed by `dpkg-deb -c target/debian/*.deb` checks the package's contents. The release build takes about 75 seconds.
summary:
This compliance check found no open CVEs, but only RustSec could run: trivy and grype aren't installed here. I fixed the one real code finding, closed the Iced-Icons font licence question, and committed everything on my branch. `cargo test --locked` passes (46 passed, 1 ignored), and `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` have no warnings.

**Scans (R34):** RustSec found 0 advisories, using a database it downloaded at 2026-11-14 05:57 UTC. That result has gaps:
- trivy and grype didn't run because they aren't installed.
- RustSec doesn't cover the git dependencies (libcosmic, cosmic-panel, window_clipboard and two others).
- OSV, NVD, CISA KEV, the Rust toolchain and the release tools weren't scanned.

I filed these gaps as **FV-YWGP02**. Whether to install trivy or grype is your call.

**CVEs:** none are open, so nothing needed upgrading or an exception.

**Code:** this was the first compliance check, so I scanned the whole tree. The smell scan found two things:
- **RS7 (fixed):** `update` in `src/main.rs` was 146 lines. I moved two of its branches into their own functions, `temperature_changed` and `reply_received`, without changing what they do.
- **RS4 (left alone):** the flag on `handle_request` is a false positive. The backend is only created when there's no connection, and the code already says so.

No issues filed and nothing for the architect.

**Docs:**
- **Iced-Icons.ttf licence (FV-J3BMZE / FV-MGVC59):** I had network access this time. I compared the font's glyphs point by point with Fontello's sources: six are Font Awesome icons, licensed SIL OFL 1.1, and one is the iced logo, licensed MIT. The OFL requires its text to ship with the font, so I added `data/licenses/OFL-FontAwesome.txt`. A `cargo deb` build shows the package now installs it.
- I replaced the "open point" in `docs/BUNDLED-ASSETS.md` with the confirmed source and licence, and the CHANGELOG now lists the licence notices the package installs.
- The README, CHANGELOG and RELEASING.md otherwise match the code.
- The project has no SECURITY.md, PRIVACY.md or AGENTS.md; I didn't create them.

**For whoever keeps the requirements:** issues refer to R14, R33 and R34, but only R0–R2 are recorded. The features list is also missing Auto (sunrise/sunset) and the .deb/apt packaging.

The commit's "Fixes" lines will close FV-J3BMZE, FV-MGVC59 and FV-X6J1CF when it merges. X6J1CF asked for the scan to be run, which is done.
